options.text: Atoms of different elements with the same mass number
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of electrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of protons

questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same number of protons) that have different numbers of neutrons, giving them different mass numbers. The number of protons cannot differ or they would be different elements. In neutral atoms, electrons equal protons, so electrons are also the same.

questions.stem: Chlorine has two isotopes: Cl-35 (75% abundance) and Cl-37 (25% abundance). What is the relative atomic mass of chlorine?
questions.explanation: Relative atomic mass = (35 x 75 + 37 x 25) / 100 = (2625 + 925) / 100 = 3550 / 100 = 35.5. The relative atomic mass is a weighted average that accounts for the abundance of each isotope. Since Cl-35 is more abundant, the average is closer to 35 than 37.

questions.stem: Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 are isotopes. Which property is different between them?
questions.explanation: Carbon-12 has 6 neutrons while Carbon-14 has 8 neutrons, so they have different masses. Both isotopes have 6 protons (defining them as carbon) and 6 electrons (in neutral atoms). Since they have the same electronic structure, their chemical reactivity is essentially identical. Isotopes differ in physical properties like mass but share chemical properties.

questions.stem: The relative atomic mass of boron is 10.8. Boron has two isotopes: B-10 and B-11. What can you conclude about the abundance of these isotopes?

options.text: B-10 and B-11 are equally abundant
B-10 is more abundant than B-11
B-11 is more abundant than B-10
You cannot determine relative abundance from this information

questions.explanation: Since the relative atomic mass (10.8) is closer to 11 than to 10, B-11 must be the more abundant isotope. The weighted average is pulled towards the mass of the more abundant isotope. Approximately 80% B-11 and 20% B-10 would give: (11 x 80 + 10 x 20) / 100 = 10.8.

questions.stem: Why do isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties?

options.text: Because they have the same number of neutrons
Because they have the same mass number
Because they have the same electronic structure
Because they have the same number of nucleons

questions.explanation: Chemical properties are determined by the arrangement of electrons, particularly those in the outer shell. Isotopes of the same element have the same number of protons and therefore the same number of electrons in the same arrangement. The different number of neutrons affects mass and nuclear stability but not chemical behaviour.
